SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: 2–3-day history of wheeze and shortness of breath.
  • Associated symptoms: dry cough, occasional difficulty finishing sentences, unable to walk to work; denies chest pain, hemoptysis, nocturnal wakening, or rest dyspnea. Initially stated “fever” but documented temperature 37 °C (see conflict).
- Past medical history: Childhood and adult asthma (intermittent); hay fever; eczema.
- Previous surgeries: Not mentioned.
- Medications:
  • Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (reported use every few weeks and before exercise).
- Social history: Non-smoker; alcohol ≈ 1 glass wine every 2–3 days; lives with partner; engineer; currently on sick leave/working from home due to breathlessness.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies (NKDA).

Objective:
- Vitals (self-reported): Temperature 37 °C. No other vitals provided.
- Physical examination: Teleconsultation – no in-person findings documented.
- Investigations: None performed. No peak-flow measurement available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Asthma exacerbation
   - Assessment: Likely mild–moderate acute asthma flare, possibly triggered by pollen (hay fever) or viral infection.
   - Differential diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory tract infection.
   - Investigations planned: Prescribe peak-flow meter; patient to record morning and evening readings for 1 week.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Salbutamol inhaler 2–4 puffs every 4 hours via spacer (dose/frequency per clinician advice; strength not documented).
     • Prescribe spacer device; pharmacist to demonstrate use.
     • Begin regular oral antihistamine (OTC; specific agent/dose not documented) for allergic trigger control.
   - Follow-up: Remote review in 1 week with peak-flow diary; earlier contact if fever develops, wheeze worsens, or symptoms escalate.

Quality checks:

• Missing but clinically expected elements:
  – Full set of vitals (HR, RR, BP, SpO₂).
  – Detailed asthma control history (peak flow baseline, recent exacerbations, steroid use).
  – Medication dose, route, frequency for salbutamol and planned antihistamine.
  – Immunization, family history not addressed.

• Internal conflicts noted:
  – Patient stated “I have a fever” yet measured temperature reported as 37 °C (afebrile).

• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional minor pauses but clinically adequate.
